We just do car camping every year, but with a family of five, space in the van becomes very limited (between clothes, tents, coolers, etc). What would you suggest as the minimum to pack for a four our find day trip?

Not op, but stove, 20lb propane cylinder, propane tree, propane hose, and lanterns, washable forks, knives, spoons, plates, and cups. A trash bag for each time you plan on leaving camp unattended. Cooler with a block of ice, this melts slower and is cooler. Pre cook and separate into gallon bags the food for each meal as much as possible. This prevents you from having to keep the cooler open in a search for the hotdogs that fell to the bottom. Two small wash buckets and soap for dishes.

Bring as many pairs of socks and undies as days that you'll be camping, and appropriate clothing for the weather.

Sleeping bags and pads appropriate for the temperature, and a tent. Toilet paper, paper towels, washcloths, hand towels, and bar soap so you can at least take a whores bath out of a tub.

And a good chair, as much as you way think sitting around the campfire on a log sounds scenic, your butt falls to sleep and you end up wishing you had brought a chair.

Im going car camping next week, so I'll probably post my load out afterwards.

Also, as you're in a van, it may be worth renting a box, or trailer to lug your supplies along, cars are meant for people, not gear. Having adequate room in the vehicle make the 5 hour ride to camp tolerable, don't make it seem like it lasts any longer than you have to.

Awesome list for anyone car camping! This is pretty much what we bring (except the propane supplies. We have a naptha stove and lantern). I never thought of the block of ice though! We just buy the bags of ice. I never thought of how much longer a block would last! And unfortunately, we don't have a trailer hitch on the van, that's why we're looking to lighten the load. I've been keeping an eye out for a cheap carrier for the roof rack though.

This is definitely an excellent reference for anyone car camping though, thanks for posting it!

It may be worth looking at having a hitch installed, even if you don't intend on towing anything. There are racks that can be installed onto the hitch which can carry some of the bulkier items. Just make sure you have the clearance necessary to enter a driveway.

There are some reasonable fabric roof racks that don't break the bank, Thule has a couple of options if the only opportunity to attach is the roof. You can put your bulky, light items, like sleeping bags and clothes, in there. But READ THE INSTALLATION INSTRUCTIONS! Most are rated to only 150lbs and that is not something that you want to lose on the highway going 70.
